editorial:
You know that feeling when you want a movie that just goes big and never apologizes for it? Moonfall is exactly that kind of ride. A mysterious force knocks the moon out of orbit, and suddenly it is hurtling straight toward Earth. You follow a disgraced astronaut, a NASA executive, and a conspiracy theorist as they race against time to stop the end of the world. The vibe is pure popcorn disaster fun, packed with huge explosions, wild science, and a story that keeps raising the stakes every few minutes.

The action is loud and fast, and the special effects look great on a big screen. Halle Berry and Patrick Wilson bring real heart to their roles, while John Bradley adds some welcome comic relief. The downside is that the plot gets pretty silly by the end, and some of the science makes no sense at all. Still, if you want a brain-off thrill ride, this delivers.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn the moon is actually a giant artificial megastructure built by ancient ancestors to protect Earth. The heroes fly inside the moon and restart its power source, which pushes it back into a safe orbit. The twist is that the moon was never natural at all. Earth is saved, and the heroes make it home safely.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves big disaster movies and wild sci-fi twists.
